title: Companion animals as relational resources: Pet attachment, pet comfort, and human relationship quality among university student pet owners
abstract: Abstract Background: Companion animals can provide attachment, comfort, and social support, but these pet-related experiences may not correspond uniformly with the quality of different human relationships. This study examined whether pet attachment and comfort from companion animals were associated with friendship and family relationship quality among university student pet owners, while also considering broader indicators of social connection and sample-level pet characteristics. Methods: Cross-sectional survey analyses included 425 university students who personally owned at least one pet. Pet attachment was assessed with the Lexington Attachment to Pets Scale and pet comfort was assessed with the Comfort from Companion Animals Scale. Friendship and family relationship quality were examined as separate outcomes. Pearson correlations and multiple linear regressions were estimated, with self-esteem and social desirability included as controls. Results: Pet attachment and pet comfort were positively associated with friendship quality and remained significant after adjustment for self-esteem and social desirability (pet attachment: β = 0.19, p < 0.001; pet comfort: β = 0.18, p < 0.001). Neither pet attachment nor pet comfort was significantly associated with family relationship quality in the full owner sample. Greater attachment and comfort were also associated with higher perceived social support and lower loneliness. Conclusions: Human-animal bonds may function as relational resources in relationship-specific rather than uniformly positive ways. Among these university student pet owners, pet attachment and comfort were consistently associated with friendship quality but not with family relationship quality overall. Future research should clarify mechanisms linking human-animal bonds to distinct human relationship domains and consistently identify a focal companion animal.
